traits.leaf_shape.note: Wikipedia Pandanus (read 2026-10-17): leaves strap-shaped, may be spiny, i.e. long and narrow (linear). Pandanus is by far the largest genus (the page gives no count; it is roughly three quarters of the family), so linear leads; lanceolate kept as sometimes for broader-bladed Freycinetia and Sararanga (not read).

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Pandanaceae (read 2026-10-17): dioecious or polygamodioecious, flowers unisexual. Pandanus and Freycinetia are dioecious (genus knowledge); polygamy is the exception.

traits.perianth.note: DELTA Pandanaceae (read 2026-10-17): no perianth in Pandanus and Freycinetia; tepals only, and queried, in Sararanga (a couple of species) of c. 700.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Pandanaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire, simple; German Wikipedia, Schraubenbäume (read 2026-10-17): large simple linear leaves.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Pandanaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins parallel; blades linear or lanceolate; plants dioecious or polygamous; ovary superior; stems woody; flowers in panicles, in racemes or in heads; perianth tepals or absent; fruit usually berry, rarely aggregate; stamens 10 to 100; carpels (1-) 80. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Pandanaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves in fact usually three-ranked, looking spiral through stem twisting; four-ranked rare. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: leaf margin spiny, prickles also on upper midrib, usually; read as {"spiny": "usually"}.

traits.bract_form.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: bract form spathe; read as "spathe".

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: flowering position terminal (rarely axillary), usually; read as {"terminal": "usually"}.

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.rosette.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: rosette terminal, leaves crowded at branch tips; read as "terminal".

traits.axis_growth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219, family Pandanaceae: axis growth sympodial; read as "sympodial".

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Pandanaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add drupe (sometimes), multiple (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219: berry or drupe, multiple in some.

traits.inflorescence.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add spike (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 218, 219: panicle, spike, raceme or pseudo-umbel of spikes or spadices.
